clue.text: Mates in position side by side

definitions.note: teams are sides, one side lined up against another side

indicators.note: putting the letters of the clue word into a new position rearranges them

explanation.surface: Friends standing next to each other in their places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in position' signals that MATES is rearranged; 'side by side' playfully defines groups that are each a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a sporting side, so several sides together are squads lined up against each other.

clue.text: Order given last month about direction to take

parts.note: DEC is short for December, the last month of the year
RE is Latin for concerning, used as about
E is the compass direction east

explanation.surface: A ruling issued late in December about which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal command issued by an authority is an order with legal force.

clue.text: Surprising vista in a back street of plants reverting to type

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the other pieces of the clue
the abbreviation for street is read from right to left
a surprising result is an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unexpected view along a back street lined with throwback plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprising' looks like an adjective for the view but signals the jumble; 'back' turns the street abbreviation round, and 'in' places the jumble between the A and that.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavism is the biological reappearance of ancestral traits, so plants showing it are throwbacks.

clue.text: The position of 20 is to supervise

definitions.meaning: 20 across is a diocesan bishop, whose post sits above a see, his diocese
to watch over and manage others' work

explanation.definitionFit: A bishop rules from above his see, and supervising is watching over work; both senses share the idea of being placed over.

clue.text: Father has tea without milk or sugar

parts.note: CHA is a British informal word for tea
plain food or drink is served with nothing added

explanation.surface: A priest likes his tea black and unsweetened.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea. 'Father' is the courtesy title of a priest, so it fits a chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman, often addressed as Father in the Catholic tradition.

clue.text: Give weight to conversation with a bird!

parts.note: a stone is a British unit of weight of fourteen pounds
a chat is an informal conversation

explanation.surface: Lending importance to a talk that involves a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European songbird of the thrush family named for its clicking call.

clue.text: To get in exercise, one must be alert

indicators.note: the short form for exercise goes inside the word for get

parts.note: to receive something is to get it
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: Anyone who wants to fit some exercise into their day must stay sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the British school term for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receptive is quick to take in ideas and impressions, so mentally alert.

clue.text: Closes the shelter in a ship

indicators.note: the shelter word is placed within the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Someone seals off the cabin on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut a door or lid is to close it.

clue.text: Silver we receive in payment for work done

indicators.note: the pronoun takes in the symbol, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: We are paid in silver coins for our labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is the regular sum an employer pays a worker for labour.

clue.text: He will get better and finish after the mischief maker-right after

indicators.note: right after says the abbreviation for right comes straight after the imp
finish after the mischief maker puts the word for finish later in the answer, at its end

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
over means finished, at an end

explanation.surface: A naughty child will mend his ways once the troublemaking is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces out of answer order; the two uses of 'after' put them back in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes things better, or who learns and progresses, is one who gets better.

clue.text: Add a couple of pages before the last bit

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: Insert two more pages just before the conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach something extra at the end, so to add it.

clue.text: Dining room in disarray

definitions.meaning: a military eating hall where service members take meals together
untidy and disordered, a state of chaos

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers eat in the mess hall, and a muddle or shambles is also a mess.

clue.text: Point to a member twiddling cane with great style

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: twiddling something turns it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gestures at a leg while gracefully twirling a walking cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is refined grace and polish in appearance or manner.

clue.text: Holds back because the seat is broken

indicators.note: something broken has its parts disordered, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to sit down because the chair is damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause through doubt, keeping oneself back from acting.

clue.text: Eastern group is not far away

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, while the answer is its superlative, closest of all

indicators.note: to group things is to arrange them, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A bloc of Oriental countries lies close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' is a verb here, rearranging EASTERN; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near means the closest, the least distance off.

clue.text: Put some money in trust not long ago

indicators.note: the coin is placed inside the word for trust

parts.note: to rely on someone is to trust them
a cent is a small coin, a sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone lately deposited funds in a trust account.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, at a time just past.

clue.text: The gossip is that a large number are in summer footwear

indicators.note: the large number is placed inside the footwear word

parts.note: a sandal is an open shoe worn in warm weather
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: The rumour going round is that crowds are wearing sandals this summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandal is malicious talk about wrongdoing, so gossip and rumour.

clue.text: Pair of birds which appear very early

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; the answer is a noun for the time at dawn

parts.note: a cock is a male fowl
a crow is a black bird

explanation.surface: Two birds turn up at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn is when the rooster calls, so the time 'at cockcrow' is very early.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockcrow is daybreak, the hour when roosters call, so a very early time.

clue.text: Pawnbroker will take article that is dirty

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pawnshop owner accepts a filthy item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means soiled, the opposite of clean.

clue.text: Deacons I ordain should be given bishop's job

indicators.note: to ordain is to order or arrange, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The deacons I ordain ought to be made bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordain' looks like church business but it signals rearranging DEACONS I.
explanation.definitionFit: Diocesan describes what belongs to a diocese, the area a bishop governs.

clue.text: Certain to make the right use of it

indicators.note: to make something out of the letters is to form them into a new word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Be sure to put it to proper use.
explanation.walkthrough: R and USE are rearranged together, 'to make' signalling the new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure is being confident and without doubt, certain.

clue.text: A hundred went to court on foot

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase pointing to something found on an animal's foot

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to go to court is to go to law

explanation.surface: A hundred people walked to the courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went to court' is going to law; 'on foot' describes where the hooked nail grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A claw is the curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal.

clue.text: Habit that gives an abstainer rage

parts.note: TT means teetotal, one who abstains from alcohol
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: A teetotaller with a temper comes out as a matter of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' is clothing, as in a monk's habit, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a costume such as a nun's robe, so it means clothing.

clue.text: Freshly dropped litter

parts.note: not rubbish just thrown down but a litter of animals newly born, dropped being the word for birth in livestock

explanation.definitionFit: Newborn offspring of an animal are its brood, the litter it has just produced.

clue.text: Lady in the rail system with a streamer

indicators.note: the woman's name is placed inside the railway abbreviation

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman on the trains carrying a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, Britain's old nationalised railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a long flag or strip of cloth flown like a pennant.

clue.text: Position two keys in a liquid

indicators.note: the two keys go inside the word for a liquid

parts.note: a lotion is a liquid preparation for the skin
C and A are musical keys

explanation.surface: Place a couple of keys in some fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a place or site, where something is positioned.

clue.text: Counts and recounts

definitions.meaning: votes are counted by an official, a teller
narrates a story or relates events

explanation.definitionFit: A bank teller or vote counter numbers things, and a storyteller narrates; both senses share the verb.

clue.text: Working for the party by serving gin cocktail

parts.note: Labour is a British political party

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Campaigning for a political party by pouring mixed drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges GIN into ING; Labour is the British left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: Labouring is toiling, doing hard physical work.
